Subject: Re: initial order form — request: move capacity and pricing hold

Thanks Chloe — quick ask from our procurement team. We need to shift 30% of the Q1 burst GPU pool in the draft order form into the reserved pool (we're expecting steadier usage). That change will affect the fee schedule in Exhibit B.

Two asks: 1) can Redwood provide a short redline showing the swap (burst -> reserved) + the resulting monthly rate impact, and 2) would Redwood hold pricing for signatures for 10 business days while we conclude finance signoff? Procurement is worried about the SOW timing and wants a pricing hold to avoid churn.

Attached a one-page note from our finance lead. Happy to hop on a short call tomorrow if that helps.

— Oliver
Procurement Lead, Medistack

Oliver — thanks for the clear ask. We can do the scope swap and produce a redlined order form that reflects: move of 30% burst to reserved, updated Exhibit B rates, and a short implementation note in the SOW about capacity allocation timing.

A couple of internal items I want to surface: 1) Jordan — legal will likely need an explicit clause for the "pricing hold" (start/end date + limited carveouts for material cost changes). 2) Rishi — can you confirm whether a 10-business-day hold is acceptable given our reserved capacity provisioning timelines? If legal or billing needs different language we should propose it now to avoid rework.

I'll draft the redline and attach v3 of the order form for review by EOD. If Medistack prefers, we can mark pricing as "firm until 2026-12-05" in the doc and leave the DocuSign envelope pending.

Thanks — Chloe
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: initial order form — request: move capacity and pricing hold

Chloe / Jordan — quick legal POV: we can accept a 10-business-day pricing hold but we need narrow guardrails: 1) a start date tied to the signature of the current order form (or mutual written acknowledgment), 2) carveout for verified material cost increases (GPU cloud pass-throughs) with 3 days' notice, and 3) a one-time limited right to rescind if provisioning capacity materially changes (we'll define thresholds).

I'll prepare redline language for Exhibit B and a short clause to append to Section 2 (Fees & Payment). Also recommend adding a short acceptance window in the SOW exhibit for scheduling the migration (keeps ops aligned).

Jordan — please advise on billing team lead to loop for the pass-through clause.

— Rishi
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Oliver — looping in our billing/ops lead, Monica. Monica: the proposed swap is 30% of the burst pool to reserved capacity starting 2027-01-01 (aligned to Medistack's Q1 ramp). Can you confirm whether that timing triggers any procurement/fulfillment constraints on our side? If the change can impact provisioning cadence we'll note it and include an implementation timeline in Exhibit C.

Oliver — we also prepared the redline language Rishi suggested and attached a redlined PDF of Exhibit B (pricing) plus the v3 docx Chloe uploaded. Please review and flag any questions. If Medistack is comfortable I can mark pricing as "firm until 2026-12-07" (10 business days from proposal date) and we will hold that rate in the DocuSign envelope until signature.

Thanks all — reviewed the redlines with our legal team this morning. A few clarifications: 1) Medistack Legal wants the hold start to be the date of the most recent order form revision (2026-11-21) rather than the signature date, and 2) they want the GPU pass-through carveout limited to "force majeure-level" cost spikes (they don't want routine cloud price changes to void the hold).

If Redwood can accept those two items we'll sign the updated order form and route to DocuSign. Otherwise we'll need a short call to align. Appreciate the quick turnaround — the updated redline looks good overall.

— Oliver
